clue.text: Tries to get new deal to redevelop one great site

indicators.note: to redevelop a site is to rebuild it in a new form, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A developer haggles afresh over plans to rebuild a prime site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redevelop' rearranges the twelve letters of ONE GREAT SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegotiating means working out fresh terms, so someone doing it seeks a new deal.

clue.text: Most of London maybe enthralled by authentic performance

indicators.note: being enthralled by something is being held captive within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: authentic means real

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: London is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A concert in the capital is captivating and genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London maybe' is a definition by example; 'Most of' drops the last letter of that city word, and 'enthralled by' sets the remainder inside the word for authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetic performance given by one or a few players.

clue.text: Arrest old boy, someone very rich

parts.note: to nab is to arrest
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Police pick up a former pupil who turns out to be a millionaire.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was originally a wealthy returnee from India, hence any very rich person.

clue.text: Like young man following advice and being destroyed

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense recalls the advice 'Go west, young man', urging Americans to settle the frontier; the second is slang for being ruined or lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the American frontier fits the famous advice; the idiom also means perishing or breaking down.

clue.text: Instructed in time past

parts.note: old means past, of former days

explanation.surface: Ordered to do something in days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Being told to do something is being instructed or ordered.

clue.text: Sort of mammal panther seems to be from what it's consumed!

definitions.text: Sort of mammal panther seems to be from what it's consumed!

parts.words: Sort of mammal panther seems to be from what it's consumed!
parts.note: the big cat's name has a small insect sitting in its middle, as if the beast had swallowed one, so it looks like an insect-swallowing animal

explanation.surface: A big cat seems to be defined by its diet.
explanation.walkthrough: P-ANT-HER visibly holds an ANT, so the panther looks as though it has eaten one.
explanation.definitionFit: This mammal of the Americas feeds on ants and termites with a long sticky tongue.

clue.text: Painter making some patterns — terrific!

indicators.note: making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist produces some splendid designs.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born surrealist painter.

clue.text: Big clubs given promises of money after spring

indicators.note: after places the spring piece at the front, with the rest following it

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Large golf clubs are funded by pledges once spring arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious means roomy or large, a synonym for big.

clue.text: A story's written about any number of immigrants maybe

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a story is a lie, so story's (story is) gives lies
N is the algebraic symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A tale is penned about a crowd of newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story's' reads as 'story is', plural LIES; 'written' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are foreigners, and immigrants are one example of such people.

clue.text: Pussy full of vivacity getting left half hidden in vehicle

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside, so the cat contains the rest

parts.note: pussy is a familiar word for a cat
brio means vivacity or liveliness

indicators.note: half of the word is out of sight, leaving only its first half

explanation.surface: A lively cat half hides itself in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pussy' looks like a passenger, but it is the cat that holds everything; 'half hidden' keeps only the front half of 'left', and 'full of' sets the liveliness and that half inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, originally a light horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Name given to stone or cactus

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone

explanation.surface: A label is attached to either a gem or a prickly plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The nopal is a prickly pear cactus of Mexico.

clue.text: To talk about old part of the Caribbean

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to gab is to talk idly

explanation.surface: Someone chatters about the history of an island region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is an island in the Caribbean, part of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Page with written piece on the electron, say

parts.note: an article is a written piece in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A page carries an essay about the electron.
explanation.definitionFit: The electron is an example of a subatomic particle.

clue.text: Bound to be hit

explanation.definitionFit: Lashed means tied down with rope, and also struck as with a whip.

clue.text: Telling off Carol when concealing ailment

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a cold is a minor ailment

explanation.surface: Carol gets rebuked for hiding that she is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name; it is the verb, to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding is a rebuke, the same as a telling-off.

clue.text: International organisation makes leftie furious

parts.note: a red is a left-wing person, a communist
cross means angry or furious

explanation.surface: An aid group enrages a left-wing activist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is a worldwide humanitarian organisation.

clue.text: Go over loch that's showing anything but turbidity

parts.note: to clear a fence is to go over it
Ness is a Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Inspecting a Scottish lake for murkiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearness is the opposite of cloudiness, the state of not being turbid.

clue.text: Judge fools, type falling short

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A judge calls people idiots but fails to measure up.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor judges values or evaluates performance, and also advises a judge in court.

clue.text: Treachery in a job, say, when badly treated

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: something badly treated is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disloyalty at work comes from someone who was poorly handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly treated' rearranges A, POST and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is abandonment of one's faith or cause, a form of betrayal.

clue.text: Holy monk finds the answer sitting on a tree

indicators.note: in a down answer, sitting on means coming above, so the first piece precedes the second

parts.note: ANS is the abbreviation for answer
an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A holy man finds enlightenment while sitting under a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: St Anselm was a Benedictine monk who became Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Not so much gold for one letting out property?

parts.note: less means not so much
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A landlord asks less gold for renting out a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor is a person who grants a lease, letting property to a tenant.

clue.text: Grounds with lodge in having buried uranium

indicators.note: having buried something means holding it underneath or within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to lodge in a place is to reside there
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A gatekeeper's cottage stands on land contaminated with buried uranium.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds are sediment such as coffee dregs, the residue left at the bottom.

clue.text: Church officials who may be working at the fringes?

definitions.text: Church officials who may be working at the fringes?

parts.words: Church officials who may be working at the fringes?
parts.note: lay helpers in a parish; read playfully, men stationed at the edges or flanks

explanation.surface: Parish helpers are imagined toiling on the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lay assistants to churchwardens who take collections and usher worshippers.

clue.text: Last thing soldiers will want, something bringing pain or destruction

definitions.text: Last thing soldiers will want, something bringing pain or destruction

indicators.note: last thing points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: hell is torment, a place or state of pain and destruction

explanation.surface: Troops dread what brings suffering and ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes an exploding artillery round, the thing troops least want to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is an explosive artillery projectile that wounds and destroys.

clue.text: Fractures bringing torment into the Civil Service

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service
to rack is to torment, as on the rack

explanation.surface: Breaks appear when torment is brought into government administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracks are fractures or splits in a surface.

clue.text: Two bean counters with zero? This'll have beans!

parts.note: a bean counter is slang for an accountant, and CA is a chartered accountant
the second accountant, another CA
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A pair of accountants with nothing find a plant full of beans.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bean counter' is slang for an accountant; CA stands for Chartered Accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao tree bears pods containing the beans from which cocoa comes.

clue.text: Climbing mount, see a stake

indicators.note: climbing in a down answer means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Etna is a mountain, a volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Climbing a mountain to view a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake a poker player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Sudden movement? You'll need breather, having little energy

parts.note: a lung is the organ one breathes with
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: To make a sudden dash, you need puff, though you have scant energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body.

clue.text: A few words to get brigand finally condemned

parts.note: a sentence is a few words strung together

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A judge's few words condemn a bandit at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sentenced is to be condemned to a punishment by a court.

clue.text: It's hard to get folk talking in Ireland!

definitions.text: It's hard to get folk talking in Ireland!

parts.words: It's hard to get folk talking in Ireland!
parts.note: read as a moan about taciturn Irish people, but really a hard object in County Cork that visitors kiss to gain eloquence

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Irish are reluctant to chat.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reverses the Irish reputation for chattiness: 'hard' means a solid stone at Blarney Castle, said to grant the gift of the gab.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing this stone at Blarney Castle near Cork is said to give persuasive eloquence.
